sentences.text: Yipetalichthys has an elaborate sliding neck joint in which a ventral laminar ridge creates a longitudinal track against the anterior dorsolateral plate.
The dermal neck joint permits measurement of the angle between the ventral laminar ridge and the skull-roof midline, which in known specimens falls into two non-overlapping ranges: ≤15° or ≥28°.
The type locality of Yipetalichthys is the Shangshuanghe Formation in China.
It was formally described in a 2026 paper in the journal Papers in Palaeontology by Zhaohui Pan and colleagues.
High-resolution micro-CT scans reveal an endocranium containing cranial nerve grooves and inner-ear structures.
Phylogenetic analysis places the order Petalichthyida as sister to Ptyctodontida and assigns Yipetalichthys to the family Quasipetalichthyidae.
A high ventral laminar ridge angle supports its placement within Quasipetalichthyidae.
The fossils come from the Eifelian stage of the Devonian period.
Researchers note that the 15–28° angle interval is currently unsampled, leaving the threshold for distinguishing neck-joint states open to future testing.
